cards.explanation: The answer is the 480th year, friends. "In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt…" Solomon began to build (1 Kings 6:1). The writer counts all the way back to Egypt, so this building day is hanging on a long, long timeline. Four hundred and eighty years is a LOT of crumbs on the counter.

The answer is False. The Bible says it was "…the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, the second month…" (1 Kings 6:1). Solomon is Israel's king, and the building began in year four, not year one. Good thing to notice, friends.

The answer is to keep all God's commandments and walk in them. God says, "…if you walk in My statutes, carry out My ordinances, and keep all My commandments by walking in them, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David." (1 Kings 6:12). Notice it's about walking, not just knowing. That's the 'if' right there. Then comes the promise.

The answer is that God will dwell among them and not abandon them. God says, "…I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel." (1 Kings 6:13). Read that slowly, friends. He doesn't say He'll visit. He says He'll dwell among them. I'd frame that line if I had a wall.

The answer is True. The text says the temple "…was finished in every detail and according to every specification." (1 Kings 6:38). Every detail, friends. Every single one. I can't even finish a batch without a few crumbs left on the counter.

The answer is seven years. The foundation went down in Solomon's fourth year, and the temple was finished in the eleventh (1 Kings 6:37-38). The text sums it up: "So he built the temple in seven years." Count it out year by year if you like, friends. I did, with my mustache.
